citation: Jyoti Srivastava, 'Three Row Houses at East Cullerton', Chicago - Architecture & Cityscape (blog), September 2009: colour photographs of 213, 215 and 217 E. Cullerton Street (East Twentieth Street before the 1930s renaming), c. 2009.
author: Jyoti Srivastava
repository: Chicago - Architecture & Cityscape (blog). Prairie library images a19-jyoti-cullerton-106, a19-jyoti-cullerton-220, a19-jyoti-cullerton-223 and a19-jyoti-cullerton-224 (stream-1900.json).
locator: Photograph 106 (217's east flank and corner oriel, from the north-east, 267 x 400 px); photograph 220 (looking west along the street past 217's east flank and oriel, 215 set back and 213's buff east flank and red front beyond, 400 x 266 px); photograph 222 (213's ground storey: the door under a pedimented hood on consoles between two framed lights, 400 x 266 px); photograph 223 (217's ground storey on the street: the oriel's copper underside, two round-headed lights and the door, 400 x 266 px); photograph 224 (215's front square-on: two round-headed lights and the round-arched door, the second storey's lights over them, behind the yard's fence, 400 x 266 px); photograph 225 (213 from across the street to the north-west: its red front under a bracketed cornice and its buff west flank and rear range, 400 x 266 px; T-3783's camera solve places it there, not north-east).
rights_note: Copyright the photographer ('(c) 2009' on some prints); the Prairie library's ruling is link only. Only what stands in the street and its forms are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-27 (T-3781) from the image store's reference copies (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a19-jyoti-cullerton-106.jpg, -220.jpg, -223.jpg), each about 400 px on its long side; -222, -224 and -225 read the same day the same way (T-3782). T-3783 (2026-11-28) brought 106, 220, 224 and 225 into data/sources/assets/cullerton_213_217_photos_t3783/ as the image gate's reference copies and solved a camera on each.
note: Modern photographs of the surviving house, about 105 years after the scene date: they show its forms, not its 1904 condition. The copper's green patina, the window grilles and the planting are 2009's; the register warns that modern grilles and patina are not proof of the 1904 state.
what_it_supplies: 217's street front: two round-headed lights under the oriel and the door in a carved stone surround west of them (223)
217's corner oriel: a rounded bay sheathed in copper over the ground storey, two storeys tall, its lights bent round it, on a rounded copper underside (106, 220, 223)
217's walls: red brick over a red sandstone base course, stone sills and heads, the ground storey's round-headed openings (106, 220, 223)
a steep gable with a finial over 217's east flank (106)

215's street front: red pressed brick, the ground storey's two round-headed lights and round-arched door in its west bay under plain stone heads, the second storey's square-headed lights on stone sills under flat stone lintels, set back behind a front yard (224)

213's street front: red, four storeys, the third storey's lights round-headed, a deep bracketed cornice (225); the ground storey's door with a transom between two framed lights under a broad pedimented hood on consoles (222)
213's east flank: buff common brick where it stands before and over 215, with lights near the front (220, 225)
213's west flank and rear range in buff common brick behind the red front, its parapet under the front's cornice (225)
what_it_does_not_supply: a 1904 date: the photographs are of the surviving house in 2009
the rear, 217's west flank, 213's west flank and the roofs behind the gable and the cornices
dimensions: no scale stands in the frame
